meta.title: Product configurator: made to order, priced as you choose · Clafina
meta.description: Options and rules for made-to-order products, worked into a price, margin, lead time and parts list, then put on a quotation. The configurator pack for Clafina.

hero.title: Every choice priced, every part counted.
hero.lede: Options and rules for products made to order, worked out into a price, a margin, a lead time and a parts list while you choose.

business.name: Oyelaran Office Furniture
business.about: An office-furniture workshop that makes desks, tables and cabinets to each customer's size and finish.

dayTitle: A day at Oyelaran Office Furniture

moments.title: One desk, many ways to make it
moments.problem: The executive desk comes in several sizes, woods and finishes, and each one costs and uses something different.
moments.handles: Tayo makes the desk configurable, with a base price, a base cost, a lead time and the bill of materials it starts from. Each option is asked as a choice, a number or yes or no, shown as buttons, a list or swatches. Each value can change the price, add lead days and add parts, in a set quantity or one worked out from other choices.

moments.title: Some choices don't go together
moments.problem: Mahogany can't take a gloss finish, and a desk with the most drawers needs to be deep enough to hold them.
moments.handles: Tayo writes rules of four kinds: not allowed, adds a part, needs, and takes longer. Each one reads as a plain sentence, and a rule can be switched off and on again.

moments.title: Checking before anyone quotes
moments.problem: Tayo wants to see the desk the way his sales staff will before they use it.
moments.handles: Try it lets him choose as a customer would, and nothing is saved. Then he publishes the product. If it is ever retired, it stays on the configurations that used it.

moments.title: Four desks in mahogany
moments.problem: Ojo and Partners want four desks in mahogany with a gloss finish.
moments.handles: Kemi chooses on Configure and quote, and the screen works the answer out as she goes: the price line by line, for one and for all four before tax, the cost, the margin, the lead time and the ready-by date. Gloss is set aside, and the screen says why.

moments.title: Not enough tops in stock
moments.problem: The workshop doesn't have mahogany tops for all four desks.
moments.handles: The bill of materials lists each part with what is needed, on hand and short, and whether it came from the base product, an option or a rule. Order the short parts opens a new purchase order with those parts and quantities filled in.

moments.title: Too big to just order
moments.problem: An order this size should go out as a quotation, not straight to the workshop.
moments.handles: Above the product's needs-a-quote amount, the screen says so. Save and put on a quotation asks for the customer, and the quotation line keeps the configuration's number. Price books, discounts and approval limits apply when it is quoted. Kemi adds notes for the workshop.

moments.title: A customer calls back to change the width
moments.problem: Mrs Nwankwo was pricing a desk yesterday and now wants it wider.
moments.handles: Saved configurations keep the exact choices, the product version and what they came to. Hers is still a draft, so Kemi changes it. A quoted one opens its quotation instead. The list has tabs with counts and updates live.

words.meaning: A product you already sell, with choices the customer makes.

Whether an option is a choice, a number or yes or no.
What a value adds to or takes off the base price: an amount or a share of the base.
How much longer a value makes the work take.
Not allowed, adds a part, needs, or takes longer, each written as a plain sentence.
Choosing as a customer would, without saving anything.
The amount above which a configuration goes on a quotation.
What the makers should know, kept with the configuration.

sharesTitle: What it shares with the rest of Clafina

shares.text: A saved configuration goes on a quotation, where price books, discounts and approval limits apply.
Each part shows what you need, have on hand and are short of.
Order the short parts opens a purchase order with the parts and quantities filled in.
A configurable product can start from an existing bill of materials, and each configuration keeps its own.

modulesTitle: The parts of Clafina a made-to-order workshop uses

faq.q: Can I stop choices that don't go together?
faq.a: Yes. A rule can rule a choice out, add a part, need another choice or add lead time. Each reads as a plain sentence, and you can switch it off and on.

faq.q: Can I check the set-up before we quote with it?
faq.a: Yes. Try it lets you choose as a customer would, and nothing is saved.

faq.q: What happens to the parts list?
faq.a: It is kept with the configuration: each part, how many, and whether it came from the base product, an option or a rule. Short parts can go straight onto a purchase order.

faq.q: What if the product changes after a quote?
faq.a: A saved configuration keeps its exact choices and the product version it was made with. A retired product stays on the configurations that used it.

faq.q: When does an order need a quote?
faq.a: You set an amount on the product. Above it, the screen says so, and the configuration goes on a quotation for a customer.

cta.title: Quote made-to-order work with the sums already done.
cta.body: Start with one product and its options. Add rules and parts as you learn what customers ask for.
